item.title: Rivers: Tinubu, Wike committed to development, says Dike
item.description: By Daniel Abia, P/Harcourt A chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Rivers State, Barr. Princewill Dike, has described Saturday’s Rainbow Coalition presidential campaign rally at the Adokiye Amiesimaka Stadium, Port Harcourt, as a defining moment in the state’s political history. Dike, who spoke with journalists shortly after the rally, said the event demonstrated political unity and the commitment of Rivers leaders and supporters to the re-election of President Bola Tinubu in 2027 and other Rainbow Coalition candidates in the state. He said the turnout of political leaders, party members, supporters and residents from across the state reflected the level of political mobilisation and support for Tinubu’s administration and the political leadership of the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike. Dike said Tinubu’s remarks on the country’s economic challenges and ongoing reforms showed the Federal Government’s determination to address structural problems inherited from previous administrations. “Tinubu is not the cause of Nigeria’s economic woes, but he is not resting on his oars in correcting the economic mismanagement of past administrations,” he said. The APC chieftain urged Nigerians to assess government policies within the broader context of national recovery and sustainable development. He said the President’s response to concerns about hunger and the rising cost of living underscored the need for deliberate reforms, responsible leadership and collective sacrifice. Dike also commended Wike for the mobilisation at the rally, describing him as a political leader whose organisational capacity, grassroots connections and understanding of Rivers politics had attracted national attention. He said Wike’s reference to the completion of the Bonny-Bodo Road, the establishment of the Federal University of Environment in Ogoniland and the appointment of at least 47 Rivers indigenes to federal positions highlighted the importance of engagement with the Federal Government. He also described Wike’s challenge to former Governor Chibuike Rotimi Amaechi to account for projects and financial transactions during his administration as significant, adding that accountability remained an essential element of democratic leadership. Dike further described Governor Siminalayi Fubara’s pledge to deliver at least three million votes for Tinubu in 2027 as a major expression of political commitment. He said the warm embrace between Tinubu and Fubara after the governor’s address symbolised reconciliation and the willingness of political leaders to work together despite previous disagreements. He urged Rivers residents, particularly youths, women and community leaders, to sustain their engagement in the political process ahead of the 2027 general elections. item.title: Asaba rally turns deadly as Delta govt, Omo-Agege trade blame
item.description: By Jimitota Onoyume THE Delta State Government and the Delta Central Senatorial candidate of the Nigerian Democratic Congress (NDC), Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, have traded accusations over the violence that erupted in Asaba on Saturday during a campaign rally by supporters of the party, leaving one person dead, several others injured and more than 30 vehicles vandalised. While the state government blamed the organisers of the rally for allegedly disregarding security advice from the police, Omo-Agege accused government-sponsored thugs of attacking the campaigners. The Commissioner for Works (Rural Roads) and Public Information, Mr Charles Aniagwu, in a statement, condemned the violence, describing the incident as unfortunate and warning that the government would not condone political violence or thuggery in the state. Aniagwu said the police had advised the organisers to shelve the proposed street march and relocate their campaign to a designated venue where adequate security arrangements could be provided. According to him, the organisers allegedly ignored the advice, resulting in a confrontation that claimed a life and left several people injured, while vehicles were damaged. He further called on the police to conduct a thorough investigation into the incident and ensure that anyone found culpable was brought to justice. However, Omo-Agege, a former Deputy President of the Senate, insisted that the NDC campaigners were attacked by thugs allegedly sponsored by the state government. In a statement by his Special Adviser on Strategy and Communications, Mr Godwin Anaughe, the former senator described the incident as an act of terror, alleging that it was not the first time NDC members had come under attack during political campaigns in the state. He recalled an alleged attack on members of his party in September this year along Airport Road in Uvwie Local Government Area when some members of his party were attacked during a rally. Omo-Agege also identified some persons allegedly involved in Saturday’s attack and appealed to President Bola Tinubu to prevail on the Delta State Government to demonstrate democratic tolerance as the country approaches next year’s general elections. He said the campaign, which attracted young people and professionals under the Obidient/OK Movement, began peacefully, with participants singing and promoting the political message of Mr Peter Obi and Dr Rabiu Kwankwaso, of the NDC. According to him, the rally remained peaceful for about 20 minutes before armed thugs allegedly descended on the unarmed participants. He said: “Young people, professionals — led by the Obidient/OK Movement — filled the streets in good spirits, singing and carrying the message of Mr Peter Obi and Dr Rabiu Kwankwaso of the Nigerian Democratic Congress, NDC. “For about twenty minutes, it was exactly what democracy should look like. item.title: Controversy: We didn’t negotiate N40,000 pay adjustment for federal workers—NLC
item.description: *Explains wage increase negotiation done by public sector unions By Victor Ahiuma-Young The Nigeria Labour Congress, NLC, has distanced itself from the negotiation of the N40,000 consequential adjustment granted to federal workers, insisting that the responsibility rested solely with the leadership of public sector unions and not the national labour centre. The Congress said the widespread attribution of the N40,000 across-the-board addition to its leadership was misleading, accusing unnamed opponents of the trade union movement of deliberately distorting the collective bargaining process to misinform Nigerian workers and the general public. In a statement yesterday by its Acting General Secretary, Benson Upah, the NLC explained that while it negotiates the national minimum wage through a tripartite arrangement involving government and employers, consequential adjustments are negotiated separately by unions in their respective sectors. The statement reads: “The Nigeria Labour Congress, NLC, has observed with grave concern the deliberate spread of falsehood and mischievous misinformation by certain opponents of the trade union movement and enemies of the Nigerian working class regarding the 2024 national minimum wage setting exercise and the consequential adjustment process. This is issued to educate the public, set the records straight, and expose the ignorance and mischief of those who seek to mislead Nigerian workers and the masses. “For the purpose of clarity, we state that the national minimum wage is set through a tripartite process involving the labour movement, the government, and employers’ representatives. The NLC’s mandate at this stage is clear and unambiguous: to negotiate the national minimum wage; the primary and basic floor below which no worker should be paid. This is the foundational wage upon which all other wage structures are built. “Once the national minimum wage has been agreed upon through the tripartite process, the responsibility for negotiating consequential adjustments; the process of aligning existing wage structures with the new minimum wage, and falling to the respective sectors. This is a fundamental principle of collective bargaining that we cannot belabour here. “In the public sector, the Joint Public Service Negotiating Council (JPSNC), comprising governmentt representatives and approximately eight trade unions with their national leadership, sit with the federal government to negotiate implementation and consequential adjustments. Its state-level counterparts negotiate with state governments. In the private sector, industrial unions negotiate individually with employers’ associations according to the dynamics of their respective sectors. “For example, the Association of Food, Beverage and Tobacco Employers (AFBTE) negotiates with the National Union of Food, Beverages and Tobacco Employees (NUFBTE) on how the national minimum wage will be applied in the food and beverage sector. item.title: Tinubu to inaugurate Kaduna-Kano rail Dec 3, says APC-PCC
item.description: Orders immediate settlement of land compensation By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council APC-PCC has said President Bola Tinubu will inaugurate the Kaduna-Kano Standard Gauge Railway on December 3, 2026, and has ordered that all outstanding land acquisition and compensation issues in Kaduna metropolis be settled immediately. The directive is meant to clear the way for the completion of the railway corridor from Abuja to Kano. Council spokesman, Dele Alake, in a statement on Sunday in Abuja said the President “is accelerating the completion of major railway projects in Northern Nigeria.” According to Alake, the President “has also directed that all outstanding land acquisition and compensation issues within Kaduna metropolis should be resolved immediately so that the railway corridor from Abuja to Kano will be completed.” The statement specifically said the “completed 190-kilometre Jaji-Kano section” of the Kaduna-Kano project and the “250-kilometre Dawanu-Kano-Kazaure-Daura-Katsina section of the Kano-Maradi project will be inaugurated by December 3, 2026.” Alake said the Kaduna-Kano line has reached “approximately 90 percent completion,” while the 400-kilometre Kano-Katsina-Maradi railway “has attained 70 percent completion.” He said both projects were far behind when the President took office. “When President Tinubu assumed office in 2023, Kano-Katsina-Maradi rail project was at barely 5% while Kaduna-Kano was less than 30% completion,” the statement said. The Kaduna-Kano line is an extension of the existing Abuja-Kaduna standard gauge line. It “will establish a continuous rail connection between Abuja, Kaduna, Zaria and Kano,” the statement said. The statement said a Federal Government team recently inspected the two projects on the President’s directive. The team was led by the Permanent Secretary of the Federal Ministry of Transportation, Engr. Funso Adebiyi. Adebiyi “expressed satisfaction with the quality of construction work, particularly the railway alignment, drainage infrastructure, embankment protection, stone pitching and soil stabilisation,” the statement said. It added that the inspection “included a train test-run journey from Jaji in Kaduna State to Kano, allowing officials to assess the completed track infrastructure and passenger comfort.” On what the lines will deliver, Alake said the Kaduna-Kano railway, when operational, “will improve passenger transportation, facilitate commercial activities and provide an alternative to road travel along one of Northern Nigeria’s busiest commercial corridors.” He said the Kano-Katsina-Maradi railway “is expected to strengthen cross-border transportation and trade between Nigeria and the neighbouring Niger Republic.” “In line with President Tinubu’s agenda, all ongoing infrastructure projects will be delivered in every part of the country as scheduled,” Alake said. item.title: “America ‘ll be back bigger, stronger’ – Trump vows after midterm defeat
item.description: President Donald Trump vowed Sunday to bounce back stronger from a massive midterm elections loss that he called a “giant step back in history” for the United States. Democrats captured both chambers of Congress in last Tuesday’s midterms that dealt historic losses for Trump’s Republican Party in states they had dominated for decades. “America took a giant step back in History with the results of the last Election,” Trump said in a post on Truth Social, saying that the stock market that had grown during his tenture took a loss after the vote. “But have no fear, we will be back, BIGGER AND STRONGER THAN EVER BEFORE!” While Republican lawmakers have been licking their wounds over the setback, Trump has sounded defiant and on Friday appointed hardline advisor Stephen Miller as his new chief of staff, signaling a bare-knuckle fightback. Democrats have pledged to hold the Trump administration to account and fight “every step of the way” against Miller, architect of Trump’s tough immigration policy. item.title: Flamingos’ Victory Not A Fluke, Performance Reflects Years Of Development – Coach Busari
item.description: Flamingos head coach Hakeem Busari has praised his players for their resilience and tactical discipline after their impressive campaign at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup, while expressing optimism about African football’s future. Busari in a post-match interview, said the performance of African teams at the tournament reflected growing quality, character and competitiveness, despite the challenges posed by strong opposition. The Flamingos became the first African team to win the competition, with goals from Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku securing the historic victory. He noted that the Flamingos had competed in a difficult group that included the defending champions, adding that the experience demonstrated the progress being made in African women’s youth football. “What we are seeing now is not a fluke. It is about development, it is about character, and it is about fighting from the beginning to really get it right. So we are elated and happy,” he said. The coach also expressed hope that more African teams would progress beyond the knockout stages in future editions of the competition and eventually reach the final. Reflecting on the Flamingos’ encounter with Japan, Busari explained that his technical crew had identified the Japanese team’s strength in winning second balls and exploiting spaces behind defensive lines. ﻿ He said the team adjusted its approach to limit Japan’s attacking opportunities, particularly by directing long balls into spaces rather than areas where the opposition could easily gain possession. Busari explained that the Flamingos initially sought to score early before adopting a more cautious approach after taking the lead, but Japan eventually found an equaliser through a set-piece situation. He described the encounter as a tactical contest that required collective defending, discipline and effective game management. According to him, the final stages of the match presented additional challenges as fatigue and anxiety began to affect the young players. Flamingos head coach Hakeem Busari celebrating the victory over Japan in the finals of the U-17 World Cup at Rabat on Saturday “The young girls are tired. We have to manage their mental scenario at that point in time. We have to manage the tactics where they need to just hustle for the ball, play fewer touches and play to the zones where the Japanese are less at home,” he explained. He identified dedication, determination and discipline as key principles that guided the team’s approach. “We need to play to our own strengths, not to the opposition’s strengths. Because if we open the game, they are quicker and they can get more one-v-ones,” he said. The coach added that the Flamingos deliberately pressed Japan to force long balls, which would give them opportunities to recover possession and launch attacks. item.title: Lagos Governorship Debate Holds At 7 P.M. Today
item.description: The Nigeria Debate Consortium, a series of debates for the 2027 general elections in Nigeria, will begin today with the Lagos governorship debate. It is the first debate in the series, organised by the consortium, which comprises Channels Television, TVC News, Punch Newspaper, The Cable, and Vanguard Newspaper, in selected battleground states ahead of the 2027 elections. The series will end with a presidential debate/townhall. ﻿ The Lagos debate will hold at 7:00 p.m. at The Hub by IALA, House of His Glory, Plot 18, Providence Road, beside Keystone Bank, Marwa, Lekki, Lagos State. The major contenders for the Lagos governorship seat include incumbent Deputy Governor Obafemi Hamzat of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), and Funso Doherty of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC). The organisers had earlier explained that the initiative would provide a credible, non-partisan platform for participating candidates to present their agendas, defend their policy choices and respond to questions on the issues that matter most to Lagos residents. It will provide an opportunity for voters to put the candidates’ capacity, ideas and priorities — from transportation and infrastructure to security, housing, education, healthcare, job creation and economic growth — under public scrutiny before the February 6, 2027, governorship elections. The Consortium assured that the debate would adhere to established professional standards, with fairness, neutrality, equal opportunity and editorial independence as guiding principles. It added that all participating candidates would be subject to the same rules, speaking times and moderation standards. Channels Television stated the event reflects the media’s responsibility to inform the electorate and strengthen democratic accountability. “Voters deserve more than campaign promises; they deserve clear answers, credible plans and an opportunity to assess those seeking their mandate. This debate will place issues, ideas and the future of Lagos at the centre of the electoral conversation. “Our responsibility is to help citizens make informed choices based on what candidates propose and how convincingly they demonstrate their capacity to deliver,” it added. Similarly, TVC News stressed the importance of issue-based engagement in the democratic process. “A governorship debate is an opportunity for candidates to move beyond political rhetoric and demonstrate the substance of their vision for Lagos,” it said. “Citizens need to understand not only what candidates promise, but how they intend to deliver. By creating a fair platform for this engagement, we are helping to promote accountability and a more informed electorate.” The debate will be broadcast to national and digital audiences through the participating media organisations’ platforms. item.title: UK lists 4 conditions migrants must meet to qualify for permanent residency
item.description: The United Kingdom, UK has introduced four mandatory conditions migrants must satisfy to qualify for permanent residency under its proposed earned settlement model, which will make obtaining indefinite leave to remain (ILR) dependent on applicants’ contributions and conduct. Under the proposed reforms, migrants will no longer qualify for permanent residency almost automatically after five years in the country. Instead, the time required to secure settled status will depend on their earnings, contribution to society and immigration history. The four non-negotiable conditions, which will apply to all applicants regardless of when they arrived in the UK, include: 1. Clean criminal record: Migrants must have a spotless criminal record, with the government proposing stricter requirements than the current rules, which allow some applicants with suspended sentences of up to 12 months to qualify. 2. High English proficiency: Applicants must demonstrate a high standard of spoken English, equivalent to A-Level English as a foreign language. 3. No outstanding government debts: Migrants must have cleared any debts owed to the UK government or taxpayer before qualifying for permanent residency. 4. Sustained National Insurance contributions: Applicants must provide evidence of sustained National Insurance contributions as proof of their economic contribution to the country. Beyond these four mandatory requirements, the proposed model introduces different settlement timelines based on migrants’ earnings and contributions. Under the arrangement, the highest earners could qualify for permanent residency after three years, while migrants earning more than £50,271 annually could become eligible after five years. Certain public service workers, including doctors, nurses and teachers, would also qualify for settlement after five years. Other migrants would be subject to a new standard settlement period of 10 years, while those who have breached immigration rules would have to wait at least 20 years before qualifying. The government said the reforms recognise settled status as a significant privilege, granting migrants unrestricted access to the labour market, the National Health Service (NHS) and the welfare system. The proposed changes are intended to make permanent residency a status migrants must earn rather than an entitlement granted after a fixed period. item.title: Vote-buying won’t work in 2027, APM candidate tells Ondo voters
item.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure The Allied Peoples Movement (APM) senatorial candidate for Ondo Central, Hon. Sunday Falae, has urged voters in Ondo State to reject vote-buying and vote according to their conscience in the 2027 general elections. Falae, who spoke in an interview in Akure, said financial inducements would not determine voters’ choices in the forthcoming elections, claiming that many Nigerians were dissatisfied with the state of affairs and wanted a change. “They can bring all the money they want, it is not going to work. I am on the streets every day and the anger is there. Look at what happened in Osun,” he said. He described what he called a “Rainbow Coalition”, a voting pattern in which individuals support candidates from different political parties for various elective positions rather than voting exclusively for one party. Falae illustrated the trend with the example of a woman who reportedly told him she intended to vote for the APC presidential candidate, him for Senate, an ADC candidate for the House of Representatives and an SDP candidate for the State House of Assembly. “People are angry and they want change. They will take the money and vote their conscience,” he said. On the management of public funds, the APM candidate questioned the accountability of state governors over increased allocations, arguing that the funds received by state governments were not reflected in the level of development across the country. “We are not holding them responsible. The amount of money they are getting does not correspond to the development we are seeing,” he said. He cited the Owena-Alade-Idanre road, which he alleged was awarded and paid for but remained unconstructed. “That road should have been constructed. That money today, we don’t know where it is. The road was not constructed and it was approved and paid. So the money went to somebody’s pocket,” he alleged. Falae argued that accountability should not be limited to the Federal Government, saying state governors, senators and local government chairmen must also explain how public funds allocated to their respective jurisdictions were spent. On the 2027 presidential election, he said the South-West should complete its eight-year presidential tenure, arguing that the contest should be between President Bola Tinubu of the APC and Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde, whom he identified as the APM’s presidential candidate. He explained that he did not join the African Democratic Congress because he did not want to campaign against Tinubu. “In all sincerity, I didn’t join the ADC because I didn’t want to campaign against the President. I want us as Yorubas to finish eight years in office. Buhari finished his eight years,” he said. Falae said he eventually joined the APM because Makinde, whom he described as a fellow Yoruba, could complete the remaining four years of the South-West’s presidential tenure. “Tinubu deserves a second term. item.title: Hashim raises alarm over 3.68m IDPs, insecurity before US commission
item.description: ABUJA — Accord Party presidential candidate, Dr Gbenga Olawepo-Hashim, has drawn the attention of the United States Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF) to Nigeria’s estimated 3.68 million internally displaced persons (IDPs), calling for greater international intervention over insecurity, religious persecution and ethnic discrimination. Hashim also called for the release of Hausa cultural activist, Maisango, whom he alleged was being unlawfully detained, and urged the international community to investigate reports of attacks and the burning of 11 villages in Shanga Local Government Area of Kebbi State. He made the appeal during an engagement with the commission on Friday, where he discussed Nigeria’s religious freedom and humanitarian challenges. According to a statement on the engagement, Hashim acknowledged that Christians in Northern Nigeria face persecution but argued that religious freedom violations also affect Muslim minorities, including Shia Muslims and Hausa communities. He said Nigeria’s religious freedom challenges extended beyond the conventional Christian-Muslim divide, alleging that ethnic identity and cultural affiliation also influenced religious and social acceptance in some communities. The Accord candidate particularly raised concerns about what he described as the marginalisation of Hausa Muslims in parts of Northern Nigeria, arguing that some communities experience unequal treatment despite sharing the same Islamic faith with other groups. On Maisango’s detention, Hashim alleged that the cultural activist had been held without trial despite reportedly being dismissed from his employment with the Department of State Services (DSS). He called for his immediate release, emphasising the need to respect due process and fundamental human rights. Hashim also cited an estimated 3.68 million internally displaced persons in Nigeria, referencing UNHCR figures as of October 2026, and argued that the humanitarian crisis cut across religious and ethnic boundaries. He specifically highlighted reported attacks on communities in Shanga Local Government Area of Kebbi State, including Kalkami, Tungar Bori and Kawara. According to him, reports of attacks in April 2026 indicated that suspected bandits killed residents, set buildings ablaze and forced inhabitants to flee their homes. He said reports that 11 villages were burnt in the area deserved sustained international attention. Hashim further alleged that some armed groups operating in the region were more interested in killing residents, destroying settlements and taking control of territory than in religious conversion. He blamed what he described as the government’s failure to adequately protect vulnerable communities and decisively confront armed groups, warning that the country’s security and religious freedom challenges must not deteriorate further ahead of another political transition. item.title: Bandits kill 12 family members, abduct others in Zamfara
item.description: By Idris Salisu, Gusau Armed men suspected to be bandits have killed 12 members of the same family and abducted several residents during an attack on Gidan Taba village in Maradun Local Government Area of Zamfara State. The attack reportedly occurred on Saturday night in Dosara Birnin Kaya Ward, with the assailants setting a room ablaze after the family members reportedly locked themselves inside to avoid being abducted. A source in the area told Vanguard that the victims belonged to the family of one Mallam Muhammadu Sani, who had gathered his relatives in a single room in an attempt to protect them from the attackers. According to the source, the bandits ordered the occupants to open the door but, after they refused, set fire around the room, killing all 12 family members. Several other residents were also reportedly abducted during the raid, although the exact number of those kidnapped could not be immediately ascertained. The 12 victims were buried on Sunday morning in accordance with Islamic rites. The attack comes amid recurring bandit attacks and security concerns along the busy Gusau-Sokoto road, where commuters have continued to face threats from armed criminals. Residents condemned the killings, describing the incident as barbaric, and called on security agencies and the Zamfara State Government to intensify efforts to protect lives and property. As of the time of filing this report, security agencies had yet to issue an official statement on the attack. item.title: Court awards N50m damages against Pararan over defamation
item.description: By Egufe Yafugborhi EFFURUN — A Delta State High Court sitting in Effurun, Uvwie Local Government Area, has awarded N50 million in damages against the proprietor of Pararan Mock News, Diamond Dietanuru Osakorigho, popularly known as Pararan, over a Facebook publication found to be defamatory against Apostle Michael Akpor. The court, presided over by Justice R.D. Harriman, also ordered Osakorigho to publish an unreserved apology to the cleric in Vanguard and The Nation newspapers within 14 days. It directed that the apology must enjoy the same prominence and circulation as the original publication. The judgment was delivered on November 6, 2026, in Suit No. EHC/91/2023. The court further restrained the defendant, his agents, privies, servants and all persons acting through him from publishing or causing to be published any further defamatory, injurious or libellous statements, videos or other materials against Akpor. It also awarded N1 million as costs of the suit. The case arose from a Facebook publication made on July 20, 2022, with the caption, “Warri Pastor Kpuf 2Keke passenger”, which the court found to be false and defamatory. Reacting to the judgment, counsel to the cleric, Austin Nyekigbe, a human rights activist, described the ruling as a significant statement on responsible social media engagement. He said the judgment reinforced the principle that freedom to use social media did not confer the right to publish false and defamatory information about others. “People must learn to verify information before rushing to publish it, particularly on social media. An injustice to one is an injustice to all,” he said. Also commenting on the judgment, a Warri-based lawyer, Mrs Eloho Avwaruroro-Okoye, who was present in court, said the decision underscored the legal consequences of irresponsible online publications. According to her, freedom of expression comes with responsibility, adding that those who publish false and damaging information must be prepared to face the legal consequences. She congratulated Akpor on his victory and commended Nyekigbe for his diligence in handling the case. The legal dispute followed allegations linking Akpor and two policemen attached to him to the July 12, 2022, killing of two persons at Ugbolokposo community in Effurun. However, Nyekigbe said police investigations subsequently exonerated his client and the two officers, identified as ASP Mesoro Victor and Inspector Ignatius Achazie. He said findings from the investigation, including witness statements, vehicle identification exercises and church CCTV footage, contradicted allegations linking the cleric to the killings. According to him, the police investigation report established that Akpor was at his church when the incident occurred, concluding that he was “going on with his religious business in the Church”. item.title: Troops neutralise suspected criminal, arrest five in Plateau
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS – Troops of Operation Enduring Peace (OPEP) have neutralised a suspected notorious criminal in Wase Local Government Area and arrested five suspected phone snatchers during a raid on a hotel in Jos North Local Government Area of Plateau State. The operations also led to the recovery of 26 mobile phones and other items suspected to be stolen, including laptops, earpods and power banks. Military sources disclosed that the suspected criminal, identified as Abubakar Ango, was arrested on November 4 by troops of Sector 2 OPEP at Kukawa village in Wase. “At about 7:20 a.m. on November 6, during interrogation, the suspect reportedly confessed to involvement in several criminal activities and agreed to lead troops to his gang’s hideouts in a village forest,” the sources said. They explained that the mission was intended to facilitate the recovery of weapons and possible arrest of other members of the gang. “However, while being escorted to the location, the suspect allegedly attempted to seize the rifle of one of the soldiers, prompting an immediate response that resulted in his neutralisation,” they said. On the Jos operation, the sources said troops of Sector 1 OPEP arrested five suspected criminals during a raid on a Hotel along Baring Road in Jos North. “The troops, while on patrol, responded to a report of phone snatching at about 9 p.m. on November 6, 2026. The stolen phone was reportedly tracked to the Hotel within the area, prompting troops to conduct a raid on the facility,” the sources said. They disclosed that the five suspects were found in possession of the tracked phone, while a further search led to the recovery of 26 mobile phones, 27 pouches, three MP devices, two earpods, an HP laptop, a knife and four power banks. “The vehicle belonging to the suspects was also towed to the headquarters of Sector 1 for a comprehensive search,” the sources added. “The suspects and recovered exhibits have been taken into custody for further investigation and necessary action,” the sources said. Confirming the two incidents, the spokesperson for Operation Enduring Peace, Captain Polycarp Chinonso Oteh, urged residents to cooperate with the military and other security agencies by providing credible and timely information to assist ongoing operations. “We urge members of the public to remain vigilant and promptly report suspicious movements and activities to security operatives,” Oteh said. He stressed that the cooperation of residents was critical to the success of ongoing efforts to combat criminal activities and restore lasting peace across Plateau State. “We assure residents of the military’s continued commitment to protecting lives and property and urge them not to hesitate to share useful information with security agencies,” he said. item.title: Man returns home after 28-yr journey walking around the world
item.description: A British adventurer, Karl Bushby, has returned to his childhood home in Hull, northern England, after completing a 28-year walking journey around the world that covered approximately 50,000 kilometres. Bushby, 57, was welcomed by his mother, Angela, outside her terraced house on Monday, November 2, 2026, beneath a banner reading “Welcome Home Son”. Hundreds of supporters had gathered in the city centre to celebrate his return before he completed the final stretch of his journey to his mother’s home. “Sorry to keep you waiting,” he joked to the cheering crowd. “Is that it, is it done?” Bushby began the expedition, known as the Goliath Expedition, in November 1998 in Punta Arenas, southern Chile. His goal was to travel around the world and return to his hometown without using any form of motorised transport to advance his journey. Carrying a tent, a few hundred dollars and a plastic camera, he initially expected the expedition to take about 12 years. His route took him north through the Americas before crossing the frozen Bering Strait from Alaska into Russia. He subsequently travelled through Mongolia and China, swam across the Caspian Sea and continued towards Europe. The journey also involved navigating the dense Darien Gap jungle between Colombia and Panama, crossing international borders and dealing with visa restrictions. Bushby was detained after entering Russia, while funding difficulties and the global financial crisis of 2008, which cost him major sponsors, contributed to delays that extended the expedition to 28 years. In the final stages of the journey, he swam across the English Channel last month, clearing one of the remaining major obstacles before walking the final distance to Hull. Speaking after his arrival, Bushby acknowledged the support he received from people and organisations across different countries. “They say it takes a village, but literally it took a world to get me here,” he said. “The kindness of strangers, so many, from individuals to nation-states, to get me back here today. I didn’t do this alone. There was a big team. The biggest team. Earth.” A feature-length documentary about his expedition is currently in production, while Bushby is expected to begin a speaking tour across England in the coming weeks. item.title: Ibom Deep Sea Port: Gov Eno Hails Tinubu’s Approval, Projects Economic Transformation
item.description: Akwa Ibom State Governor, Umo Eno, has described President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s approval of financing arrangements for the Ibom Deep Sea Port as a defining moment in the state’s economic development. He stated this in a statewide broadcast following the President’s visit to Akwa Ibom on Friday, November 6, during which he announced approval for the project. Governor Eno said the deep seaport would serve as a gateway to economic transformation, opening up opportunities in international trade, investment, industrial growth and employment. He expressed confidence that the project would reposition Akwa Ibom as a major economic and maritime hub in Nigeria and the Gulf of Guinea. Governor Eno thanked President Tinubu for his confidence in the state and commitment to national development, assuring him of the Akwa Ibom State Government’s full cooperation towards the successful realisation of the project. ﻿ He described the approval as a significant step in the state’s economic journey and said the government recognised the responsibility that came with the opportunity. The governor also commended residents for their participation in the President’s visit, noting that the reception reflected Akwa Ibom’s reputation as a peaceful, welcoming and investment-ready state. He expressed appreciation to traditional rulers, religious leaders, political stakeholders, youths, women, security agencies, public servants, students and other groups who contributed to the successful hosting of the President. On the forthcoming 2027 general election, he pledged that Akwa Ibom people would support President Tinubu at the polls on January 16, 2027, as part of efforts to ensure continuity in the administration beginning May 29, 2027. He ended the broadcast by thanking the President for his support and urging residents to remain committed to the state’s development, declaring: “Together, we will ARISE, build and prosper.” The post Ibom Deep Sea Port: Gov Eno Hails Tinubu’s Approval, Projects Economic Transformation appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: 2027: Tinubu delayed tax collection over fear of election – Kwankwaso warned
item.description: Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse ‎ ‎The Vice-Presidential candidate of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, has alleged that President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s administration delayed the collection of taxes under the newly enacted tax laws for fear of losing the 2027 general election. ‎ ‎Kwankwaso made the allegation while speaking at the inauguration of the NDC campaign council in Jigawa State, held in Dutse, the state capital. ‎ ‎He claimed that although the tax reform bills had been passed into law, the Federal Government was reluctant to commence their implementation because of concerns over the possible political consequences ahead of the elections. ‎ ‎“The bill has been passed into law, but the Federal Government is now afraid of losing the election. That is why it has delayed the collection,” he said. ‎ ‎Kwankwaso warned that Nigerians could face increased tax collection if the ruling party secures another electoral mandate in 2027. ‎ ‎“As soon as they get a second chance, God forbid, Nigerians will suffer from different kinds of tax collection. They will start going from house to house, checking even under your bed to collect taxes,” he added. ‎ ‎“The worst part of it is that the session for the approval of the tax bill was chaired by one of us from Kano. Even the Senate President intentionally refused to attend because he did not want to be part of it,” Kwankwaso alleged. “NDC is there for Nigerians, when you give us your mandate we will cancel all such unnecessary taxes, we will provide quality education and sponsor your child’s education” ‎ ‎Kwankwaso urged Nigerians not to give second chance to All progressives Congress, APC saying that, re-election of APC is joepadizig the future of the country. item.title: 2027: ADC will be on the ballot; Atiku may not – Keyamo
item.description: Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, has said the African Democratic Congress (ADC) will participate in the 2027 general elections despite the court ruling voiding the party’s David Mark-led leadership and the nomination of former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar. Keyamo, however, said candidates nominated under the Mark-led faction, including Atiku, might not appear on the ballot, depending on the final decision of the Supreme Court. The minister stated this in a post on X on Sunday while reacting to concerns that the Federal High Court judgment could prevent the ADC from participating in the elections. “For the education of the public, those raising false alarm that the court judgment on ADC means the Party will not be on the ballot are spreading misinformation,” he wrote. “The ADC will be on the ballot. It is the David Mark faction of candidates, including Atiku Abubakar, that may not be on the ballot, depending on the final judgment of the Supreme Court.” The Federal High Court in Abuja had, on Thursday, nullified the Mark-led leadership of the ADC and invalidated decisions taken by the faction, including the presidential primary that produced Atiku as the party’s candidate for the 2027 election. The party has vowed to appeal the judgment. Keyamo questioned why some Nigerians were protesting the ruling, arguing that the court’s decision should not be interpreted as denying the ADC’s original members the opportunity to contest elections. He challenged those criticising the judgment to consider the rights of candidates who emerged from the party’s original leadership structure. “Therefore, the question we must ask those raising hell is that, are those Nigerians who successfully won their primaries under the faction of the original owners of the ADC lesser humans or lesser Nigerians than David Mark and Atiku Abubakar?” he asked. The minister’s comments come amid uncertainty over the ADC’s participation in the 2027 elections following the court’s decision. Atiku and the ADC have rejected the ruling and announced plans to challenge it at the Court of Appeal. item.title: Delta APC decries political violence, emphasises healthy political competition
item.description: Dr Tonye Timi, an official of the Delta All Progressives Congress (APC) Campaign Council, has condemned the violence that trailed Saturday’s road procession by supporters of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), along Nnebisi Road, Asaba. Timi, Secretary, Media and Publicity Committee of the campaign council, described the development as unfortunate and a troubling reminder of the dangers of allowing political differences to degenerate into violence. The official, in a telephone interview with Newsmen Sunday, warned that Delta must not become a theatre of political violence. “This incident remains condemnable and I share my heartfelt sympathy with the family of the deceased, those who sustained injuries and all others affected by the unfortunate occurrence,” he said. The violence occurred around 12:15 p.m. during a road procession organised by the Obi/Kwankwaso(OK) Movement in support of the NDC and its presidential candidate, Mr Peter Obi. The Police Command in Delta has confirmed the death of one person during the clash. It also confirmed that five others were injured during the fracas. Timi emphasised that the sanctity of human life must remain paramount and no political ambition, disagreement or contest for power could justify the loss of innocent lives or the destruction of property. “The unfolding political activities ahead of the 2027 general elections should provide an opportunity for healthy democratic competition, robust engagement and the presentation of alternative visions for the development of Delta. “Nothing should create an atmosphere of hostility, intimidation and insecurity,” he said. He explained that the APC had commenced its campaign preparations and had, at the inauguration of the state campaign council, made a clear commitment to peaceful and issue-based campaigns. “This position remains sacrosanct; political parties should seek the people’s mandate through the strength of their ideas, records of performance, policy proposals and capacity to deliver good governance,” added.
